nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt + lowres video)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the location in <Picture 1> showing the layout of a professional foley setup in a backlot soundstage. 
<Subject 2> is the middle-aged man with short hair whose character reference comes from <Picture 2>.
<Subject 3> is the middle-aged man with curly hair and a beard whose reference comes from <Picture 3>.
<Audio 1> is the full audio track of a scene that <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> are doing foley work for and will be a reference for sound effects they create in the target video.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] Live-action, cinematic, documentary style, the target video shows <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> in the soundstage location shown in <Subject 1> creating foley effects for the sound effects referenced in <Audio 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (location for [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the professional soundstage, the foley equipment, the computer cart and various microphones and sound equipment are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the man's green jacket, headphones, jeans, and facial features are fully retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - the man's rust shirt, navy t-shirt underneath, jeans, curly hair and beared face are fully retained.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the effects from <Audio 1> including the multiple thunderclaps and the continuous rain are reused directly 1:1 without copying the musical score.

detailed_description: 
The target video is in a live-action cinematic realism documentary style, with slightly underexposed lighting and a slightly desaturated color palette.
[Shot 1] A medium long shot establishes <Subject 1>, the crowded foley soundstage, where <Subject 2> is preparing to manipulate a thick piece of metal to make a thunderous sound. The movement of the metal synchronizes perfectly with <Audio 1> to demonstrate <Subject 2>'s creation of the sound effect. 
[Shot 2] At 00:02.600 the shot cuts to a close-up of <Subject 3>, who is pouring small beads down a long chute to create a rain sound. 
[Shot 3] At 00:04.000 the shot cuts to a dutch angle, canted angle, tilted horizon, diagonal shot, disorienting, focused on <Subject 2>. He now manipulates the metal sheet again, in conjunction with the double-stutter of lightning in <Audio 1>.

overall_soundscape:
Sound of heavy rain on pavement throughout, increasing in volume during [Shot 2] when its creation is shown. The first thunder is in [Shot 1] is deep, loud, and sustained, panning from right to left, preserving exactly the first thunder sound from <Audio 1>. The second thunder is a cra-crack, double hit, not as loud as the first lightning overall but the second crack builds intensity over the first, preserving exactly the second thunder from <Audio 1>

non_diegetic_music: 
N/A

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing the young woman standing in the rainy backlot street. 
<Subject 1> is the young blonde woman whose facial and character reference comes from <Picture 2> and who appears as the primary subject in <Picture 1>, with wet blonde hair and the tattered, dirty light dress and bare feet.
<Audio 1> is the non-diegetic music track for the shot.

summary:
[keyframe completion + reference generation + audio reuse] Live-action, cinematic, the target video shows <Subject 1> scared in the street, rain falling hard, lightning striking behind her, startling her, then building her resolve.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the backlot street, building facade, pouring rain, and scared young woman are retained.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the blonde woman's identity, wet hair, tattered dress, and bare feet are retained.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the beginning of <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final non-diegetic music track.

detailed_description: 
The target video is in a live-action cinematic horror realism style, underexposed dark lighting and a slightly desaturated color palette.
[Shot 1] The shot's keyframe corresponds to <Picture 1>. the young woman <Subject 1> stands as shown in <Picture 1> in the backlot street, preserving her appearance, clothing, and location. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her face as rain falls. Lightning flashes in the sky high frame-right, momentarily lighting the entire scene brightly and she flinches in response to it. 
[Shot 2] At 00:02.600 the shot cuts to a close-up of <Subject 1>, capturing the fear in her eyes and her heavy breathing and startled reaction as the thunder follows the lightning. Rain continues.
[Shot 3] At 00:04.000 the shot cuts to a dutch angle, canted angle, tilted horizon, diagonal shot, disorienting, focused on <Subject 1>. A second, double-stutter of lightning fires, a bit higher and further away, weaker and shorter than the first, silhouetting the facades again. Her fear heightens as she prepares to run. The rain intensifies.

overall_soundscape:
Sound of heavy rain on pavement throughout. The first thunder is deep, loud, and sustained, panning from right to left, slightly delayed behind the lightning. The second thunder is a cra-crack, double hit, not as loud as the first lightning overall but the second crack builds intensity over the first. The character's breathing is close and centered throughout, fast and unsteady.

non_diegetic_music: <Audio 1> is directly reused as the complete audience-only score.
